note: One entry per clip. 'segments' is the narration: one line per on-screen caption, in the order the captions appear in the scene.

segments.caption: A 2026 LLM is still a stack of decoder blocks, like the 2017 transformer.
segments.text: A large language model in twenty twenty-six is still a stack of decoder blocks, much like the twenty seventeen transformer: attention, then a feed-forward network, each with a residual connection.

segments.caption: Normalization moves before each sublayer and becomes RMSNorm.
segments.text: The first change is normalization. It now comes before each sublayer instead of after, and it uses R M S norm, which only rescales each vector by its root mean square.

segments.caption: The feed-forward network becomes SwiGLU, a gated version.
segments.text: Second, the feed-forward network becomes swig-loo. The token is projected twice, and one projection passes through a smooth activation and acts as a gate on the other.

segments.caption: Positions move inside attention: RoPE rotates each query and key.
segments.text: Third, positions are no longer added at the input. Instead, rope rotates every query and key inside each attention layer, as we saw in week two.

segments.caption: Attention becomes grouped-query attention: query heads share keys and values.
segments.text: Fourth, attention becomes grouped-query attention. In the small Kwen three model, sixteen query heads share eight key and value heads, which saves memory during generation.

segments.caption: The shape is unchanged: stack the blocks, then predict the next token.
segments.text: The overall shape is unchanged. The twenty seventeen decoder stacked six blocks, the small Kwen three model stacks twenty-eight, and the last block feeds the prediction of the next token.

segments.caption: Each new token needs the keys and values of every earlier token.
segments.text: When a decoder writes the next token, its query is compared with the keys of every earlier token, and their values are mixed in. Here the note so far is: the patient denies chest pain.

segments.caption: The model stores them instead of recomputing them: the KV cache.
segments.text: Those keys and values do not change, so the model stores them instead of recomputing them at every step. This store is the K V cache, and each new token adds its own keys and values.

segments.caption: The cache grows with every token, in every layer and every head.
segments.text: The cache grows with every token, in every layer and every head. For a model shaped like Llama three, eight B, that is half a megabyte per token, so a patient record of thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-eight tokens needs sixteen gigabytes.

segments.caption: Grouped-query attention: 8 key/value heads instead of 32, a 4× smaller cache.
segments.text: Grouped-query attention shrinks it. Thirty-two query heads share eight key and value heads, so only eight are stored, and the same record needs four gigabytes instead of sixteen.

segments.caption: Latent attention (DeepSeek-V3) caches one small compressed vector per token.
segments.text: DeepSeek V three goes further with multi-head latent attention. It caches one compressed vector of five hundred seventy-six numbers per token and layer, instead of forty thousand nine hundred sixty: about seventy-one times smaller.

segments.caption: Sliding-window attention: most layers look only at the most recent tokens.
segments.text: Sliding-window attention is a third approach. In Gemma three, the base of Med Gemma, five local layers look only at the last one thousand twenty-four tokens for every global layer that sees everything.

segments.caption: In a dense model, every token goes through the same feed-forward network.
segments.text: In a dense model, every token passes through the same feed-forward network, and all of its weights are used for every token.

segments.caption: A mixture of experts splits it into many smaller networks, called experts.
segments.text: A mixture of experts splits this network into many smaller networks, called experts. Here we draw sixteen of them, and the numbers in this clip are illustrative.

segments.caption: A router scores the experts for each token and picks the top two.
segments.text: A small router scores every expert for each token. For chest, experts three and eleven score highest, zero point three eight and zero point two five, so only those two run.

segments.caption: Different tokens go to different experts.
segments.text: Other tokens are routed to other experts: denies to experts one and nine, and pain to experts seven and fourteen. Experts that no token chose stay idle.

segments.caption: Each token's output is a weighted sum of its chosen experts.
segments.text: The output for chest is a weighted sum of its two experts: zero point six times expert three, plus zero point four times expert eleven. The router weights are rescaled to sum to one.

segments.caption: DeepSeek-V3 has 671B parameters in total, but uses only 37B for each token.
segments.text: DeepSeek V three has two hundred fifty-six experts plus one shared expert in each layer, and picks eight per token. It has six hundred seventy-one billion parameters, but uses only thirty-seven billion for each token.

segments.caption: Bigger vocabularies: the same clinical note in fewer tokens.
segments.text: Vocabularies have grown. G P T two, from twenty nineteen, splits this clinical sentence into twenty-one tokens and cuts tachycardia into four pieces. DeepSeek V three, with about one hundred twenty-nine thousand tokens in its vocabulary, needs only fourteen.

segments.caption: Longer context: train on short text, then stretch the RoPE angles.
segments.text: Long patient records need long context. A model is trained on shorter text; rotating eight times slower lets position thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-eight land where four thousand ninety-six was. DeepSeek V three was stretched from four thousand to thirty-two thousand, then one hundred twenty-eight thousand tokens.

segments.caption: Multi-token prediction: in training, also predict the token after next.
segments.text: Multi-token prediction adds a second target during training. From the patient denies chest, the main head predicts pain, and an extra module predicts the token after next: and. This gives more training signal and can speed up generation.

segments.caption: MedGemma: Gemma 3 adapted to medical text and images.
segments.text: This week's paper, Med Gemma, starts from Gemma three and continues training on medical text and medical images. It comes in four billion and twenty-seven billion parameter versions, built from the pieces in these clips.
